lesson.title: Skit Day: Performing Formal and Informal Greetings
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: All week you've been building toward this: today you perform a complete greeting-and-goodbye conversation, once informally and once formally, as a two-person skit.

[[despedirse]] means 'to say goodbye' — just as important as saludar for a complete conversation, since every greeting eventually needs a matching exit. Goodbyes change with the register exactly the way hellos do: an informal goodbye is short and casual (Chao, ¡Nos vemos!), while a formal goodbye is a little more polished (Hasta luego, Que tenga un buen día). Before you perform, think back through the whole week: tú for people you're close to, usted for people you're showing respect to, ustedes for any group, and now saludar and despedirse as the two halves — hello and goodbye — that frame every conversation you'll have in Spanish this year.

Perform both skits out loud with a family member playing the second role — or play both parts yourself, changing your voice for each character.

SKIT 1 — INFORMAL (dos amigos):
MARTA: ¡Hola, Diego! ¿Cómo estás?
DIEGO: Muy bien, gracias. ¿Y tú?
MARTA: Bien también. Oye, ¡nos vemos mañana!
DIEGO: ¡Sí, hasta mañana! Chao.

SKIT 2 — FORMAL (un estudiante y la directora):
ESTUDIANTE: Buenos días, señora Vargas. ¿Cómo está usted?
SRA. VARGAS: Muy bien, gracias. ¿Y usted?
ESTUDIANTE: Bien, gracias.
SRA. VARGAS: Que tenga un buen día.
ESTUDIANTE: Igualmente. Hasta luego.

Notice how the goodbye lines change with the register too, exactly like the greetings did: Chao is casual and quick; Hasta luego and Que tenga un buen día sound more polished and complete.

You've now greeted someone, asked how they're doing, and said goodbye — twice, in two different registers, entirely in Spanish. That's a real conversation. Next week, you'll use these same greeting skills to start talking about identity and where people are from.

objectives: Perform a complete greeting-to-goodbye exchange from a script in both the informal and formal registers
Identify how goodbye phrases (Chao vs. Hasta luego / Que tenga un buen día) shift with register, the same way greetings do
materialsNeeded: A family member to play the second role in each skit
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review the week: tú/usted/ustedes and saludar, introduce despedirse as saludar's counterpart.
2. Read Skit 1 (informal) together, then perform it with roles assigned.
3. Read Skit 2 (formal) together, then perform it with roles assigned.
4. Swap roles and perform both skits again.
5. Complete the worksheet.
6. Preview next week's topic: identity and nationality.
differentiationTips: Struggling: perform each skit reading straight off the page first; only attempt it from memory on a second pass once the lines feel familiar
Ready for more: have them write and perform a third short goodbye-only exchange (no greeting, just parting) in either register, using despedirse's vocabulary as inspiration
Recording the performance (phone video) gives a low-stakes way to review pronunciation together afterward, without the pressure of a live audience
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. Diego asks Marta ¿Cómo estás?, using the informal tú-form. 2. Usted (in ¿Cómo está usted?) tells you Sra. Vargas is being addressed formally. 3. Any short, casual goodbye is acceptable — e.g. Chao, or ¡Nos vemos! 4. Any polished, formal goodbye is acceptable — e.g. Hasta luego, or Que tenga un buen día.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Closes the week's WA-WL-2015.1.1 Interpersonal Communication arc with Presentational-style output — a full memorized exchange performed start to finish — which is exactly the 'memorized frames' starting point the Spanish 6-8 band notes call for before the course moves toward original sentence construction in later weeks.

generationData.instructions: Answer each question using Skit 1 and Skit 2 from today's lesson.

rows.problem: In Skit 1 (informal), which word does Diego use to ask Marta how she's doing?
In Skit 2 (formal), which word tells you Sra. Vargas is being addressed formally?
Write your own one-line informal goodbye, like the ones in Skit 1.
Write your own one-line formal goodbye to a teacher, like the ones in Skit 2.
